cells.tense: You are still here, at the end of what you started, working the pattern.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Stand firm in the pressure that's actually on you this week. Pick the hard thing you're already carrying and hold it without fixing, quitting, or renegotiating it.
cells.core:
Endurance is the oldest thing you do, and it's still working. You've kept at something long enough that its shape shows through the details now — you can see the mechanism underneath, not just that it holds, and that reading is what steadies the next push. Nothing here is forced. You bear the weight because it's yours, and you bear it honestly.

Stand firm in the pressure that's actually on you this week. Pick the hard thing you're already carrying and hold it without fixing, quitting, or renegotiating. Stay on your own reserves; don't spend the day checking whether anyone noticed. The hardness is where you're steadiest, and standing in it shows you that.
cells.sheetLine: You can see how it works and keep carrying it anyway.
cells.verb: Continuing to hold a course long after the first reason for it has gone
cells.place: Where a thing is seen as pure pattern, with its content stripped away

cells.tense: You will be braced for a weight that has not arrived yet, jaw set early.
cells.act: write both sides of it on one page and close the page
cells.ask: Put both readings of one situation on a single page, then shut the page without choosing. Don't say the answer to anyone, or to yourself.
cells.core:
Endurance went past its mark. You're bracing for the next load before it's here, holding a line against things that haven't happened, and what you used to read quietly you're now announcing early. Two readings of the same situation are both being held, and neither gets to sit down. That's not strength anymore; it's a stance held past the moment it was for.

Put both readings of one situation on a single page, then shut the page without choosing. Where you'd normally settle it or say the answer first, let both stay true. Keep it off the record, not even as a verdict you hand yourself. The grip relaxes when the answering waits. You'll know what's true after the pause, and it won't need announcing.

cells.tense: You were standing at that door long after the room behind it went quiet.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Tend one real thing — a plant, a bill, a person who is here. Give it what it actually needs, not the amount you'd give something else.
cells.core:
The endurance is there; the reason it was for has gone quiet. You're holding a shape that ended, still at the door, still working the pattern, and the work has become its own task rather than the thing it was for. Seeing how things work is what you do best, and right now what you're seeing is a long hallway with nobody coming down it.

Tend one real thing — a plant, a bill, a person who is here. Give it what it needs, in the amount it actually needs, not the amount you'd give something else. That kind of tending doesn't need a big hope behind it, and it will tell you what's still alive to put your weight on.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping a promise to something that already ended.

cells.tense: You are carrying the load steadily while telling yourself it is only habit.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Go through the hard stretch without asking whether you're doing it right. Don't poll anyone, don't report in. Just do the thing you do when it's heavy.
cells.core:
You've been holding through the hard part for as long as anyone can remember, and you wouldn't name it as strength. It's just what you do, you'd say — routine, not endurance. Strength runs quietly in you like this: the load lands, you take it, and the day keeps its shape. The pattern is plain in your life. Reading it back is the part you skip.

Go through the hard stretch without asking whether you're doing it right. Don't check for confirmation, don't poll anyone, don't report in. Just do the thing you do when it's heavy. You'll feel the strength in the middle of it, where you usually stop noticing. That strength is real, and it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: What you name as habit is strength you haven't counted.

attempts.check: The draft's unsupported claim is that the person's persistence is driven by a specific hope or star they chose — the record says strength from continued hoping but not what that hope is, so every cell stays off the content of it. A reader could reasonably say the Too Much cell describes ordinary caution rather than bracing; the ask (holding a thing for two days) still teaches something even if the read is wrong, since anyone learns what their own knowing is worth by waiting once. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you can read the pattern' — cut, because it praises a method rather than describing what the seat is doing, and the Too Much cell now bends the mechanism instead.
